exposure: Cesarean delivery before the scheduled date
cohort: 316 infants delivered by elective cesarean section at a single center over an 18-month period (272 delivered as scheduled and 44 delivered earlier)
finding: No significant differences in neonatal morbidity were found between infants delivered by elective cesarean section as scheduled and those delivered earlier than planned, suggesting the current recommendation to postpone elective cesarean deliveries beyond 38-39 weeks of gestation whenever possible remains appropriate.
mod_finding: The study investigated neonatal outcomes of elective cesarean deliveries scheduled at or after 39 weeks of gestation compared to those requiring earlier delivery.
